scores.evidence: Critical path: S1/S2 → schema v1 freeze → persistence + authz in Sync → multi-node → 2× load test → beta
scores.rationale: Tasks are ordered by dependency (infra/schema/db → sync → clients → spikes), and multi-node, versions and features wait until convergence and persistence are proven.

scores.evidence: M1: Walking skeleton + core risks ... Two users in staging co-edit one doc ... CI/CD to staging
scores.rationale: M1 is a real deployed end-to-end slice with login, co-edit and Postgres persistence through CI/CD before features.

scores.evidence: D1 ... Revisit if: S1 finds divergence we can't fix, or we need server-validated edits or permissions on parts of a document.
scores.rationale: Decisions D1–D8 each list options, a default, reversibility and a revisit trigger, and assumptions are tabled with validation timing.

scores.evidence: Critical path: S1/S2 → schema v1 freeze → persistence + authz in Sync ... schema v1 ... the hardest decision to undo
scores.rationale: The widest-impact items (schema, infra, DB, sync core) are built and spiked before leaf features such as presence, comments and export.

scores.evidence: Security (Milestones 1–3): JWT verified ... Dependency scanning in CI from Milestone 1.
scores.rationale: M1 has auth, membership checks and dependency scanning, but most threat mitigations (viewer read-only, revocation, limits, XSS) land in M2 and the pentest in M3, so coverage is uneven across phases.
M1 has T12 baseline logs, metrics and a save-failure alert, but the canary and full alerts come in M3 and M2 has no explicit observability task.

scores.evidence: Terraform under infra/, ... Runs and rolls back in CI against a clean Postgres (testcontainers)
scores.rationale: Terraform, pinned versions, a single image and seeded sim fuzz with repro seeds give reproducibility, but it isn't explicitly carried through each phase.

scores.evidence: Killing one of two Sync instances with 20 simulated clients: all reconnect in under 10 s, 0 lost ops.
scores.rationale: Failure handling appears in M1 (SIGTERM drain, deploy-under-load, DB-loss alert, chaos), M2 (instance kill, backoff) and M3 (restore drill, runbooks).

scores.evidence: AI-specific: doesn't apply, because there are no AI features in scope.
scores.rationale: The plan explicitly declares the AI layer N/A and adds no AI components.

scores.evidence: Routing each document to one Sync instance | S3 or the M2 load test fails, or more than 5k connections
scores.rationale: Section 17 lists deferred items, each with a concrete trigger, plus the deliberate shortcuts and the per-milestone out-of-scope lists.

note: A strong, well-ordered plan with a real walking skeleton, explicit decision gates and deferral triggers. Security and observability are only partly threaded, because key controls and alerts arrive in M2–M3.
